classification.difficultyReason: Combine input and output absolute-value transformations and distinguish smooth turning points from sharp reflected zeros.

inlines.text: . All four zeros and the central maximum are sharp points.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f(x)&=x^2-4x+3\\f(x)&=(x-1)(x-3)\\f(x)&=(x-2)^2-1.\end{align*}$$
The base parabola has zeros $1,3$ and vertex $(2,-1)$. Keep its right half and reflect a copy across the $y$-axis to obtain $y=x^2-4|x|+3$. Reflect the portions below the $x$-axis upwards. The final graph has zeros $\pm1,\pm3$, smooth local maxima $(\pm2,1)$ and a sharp local maximum $(0,3)$.

spec.description: Even reflected quadratic with four sharp zeros, two smooth humps and a central sharp peak.
spec.mathematics: y=abs(x^2-4*abs(x)+3); zeros +-1,+-3; smooth local maxima (+-2,1); sharp central local maximum (0,3).
